summary: This Part II builds the finite integral dominance and diagram-folding direction above the existing root-system roadmap. It supplies one integral order, the Stembridge step, all finite orbit-sum folds including adjacent even A and component cycles, and the invariant coroot-step export with central directions retained. Two independent routed directions receive exhaustive split briefs and stable item assignments rather than incomplete mathematical nodes.

nodes.title: Integral root dominance
nodes.statement: For x,y in the weight space, RootLE(Δ,x,y) means y−x ∈ TauCeti.posRootCone(Φ,Δ). On L this is integral root dominance. Coroot dominance is this very definition for the flipped pairing and flipped base. No global order instance is imposed on the ambient module.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
proofSteps: Wrap the existing additive submonoid; reflexivity and transitivity use zero and addition in it.
Pointedness gives antisymmetry. Simple-root independence gives the coefficientwise criterion when both differences are in Q.
Restrict to L or its σ-fixed subgroup without changing the cone. The rational cone is used only for a comparison implication.

sources.match: The order uses nonnegative integral coroot sums and retains the cocharacter lattice congruence.

acceptance: No saturation of the root lattice is introduced.

nodes.title: Stembridge positive-root step
nodes.statement: For distinct dominant integral λ,μ∈L with RootLE(λ,μ), there is β∈Φ⁺ with λ+β dominant and RootLE(λ+β,μ). Consequently λ<_Qλ+β≤_Qμ. This assertion remains valid in an ambient weight space with central directions: its proof uses only the simple-coroot tests.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
proofSteps: Write μ−λ=Σ n_i α_i. Positive roots with coordinates m_i≤n_i form a finite nonempty set: a simple root with n_i>0 belongs to it. Choose a maximal member β in the integral root order.

For each simple α_i, maximality implies either β+α_i is not a root or m_i=n_i. If the sum is not a root, the contrapositive of the obtuse-sum lemma, with the nonopposite-root hypothesis checked, gives ⟨β,α_i∨⟩≥0.
If m_i=n_i, write λ+β=μ−Σ_(j≠i)(n_j−m_j)α_j and use dominance of μ and nonpositive off-diagonal Cartan entries. This proves every simple-coroot inequality.
The remaining coefficients n_i−m_i give the upper bound; β is positive and nonzero, so pointedness makes the lower bound strict. Integrality and membership in L follow from Q⊆L.

sources.match: Dominant endpoints with an integral positive-coroot difference admit a positive-coroot step; the proof chooses a maximal eligible root.

acceptance: All positive-root and finiteness hypotheses used in choosing a maximum are explicit.
A2 λ=0, μ=α1+α2 admits the highest root; either simple root alone fails dominance.
For the coroot version apply the same argument to the flipped pairing; PGL2 does not admit the increment 1.

nodes.title: Distinct root-orbit sums
nodes.statement: For a based automorphism σ of Φ and α∈Φ, OrbitSum(σ,α)=Σ_(β∈Oσ(α)) β, where Oσ(α) is the SET of distinct iterates. It lies in E^σ. Repeated elements of a chosen period are discarded before summation. For simple orbits O write β_O=Σ_(α_i∈O)α_i.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
σ preserves Δ and L. On the root span it has finite order because it permutes a spanning finite set.
proofSteps: Take the finite set of iterates of the existing index permutation and sum the root vectors.
The permutation σ cycles that set, proving invariance; changing the representative leaves the set unchanged.
For positive α, all orbit members are positive; their coefficient sums are nonnegative and not all zero, so the sum is a nonzero member of the existing cone.

nodes.title: Folding with orthogonal simple orbits
nodes.statement: Assume Φ is finite and simply laced and any two distinct simple roots in one σ-orbit are orthogonal. On E^σ, the set Ψ={OrbitSum(σ,α):α∈Φ}, with duplicates removed, is a finite reduced crystallographic root system with base B={β_O:O a simple orbit}. The form is the restricted canonical positive form, with positive componentwise rescaling constant on σ-cycles when normalizing lengths. Such rescaling leaves all coroot pairings unchanged. With original roots normalized to squared length 2, (β_O,β_O)=2|O| and ⟨β_O,β_T∨⟩=−N_OT/|T| for O≠T, where N_OT counts edges between the two blocks.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
Φ is simply laced on each component, with the normalization constant across components permuted by σ.
Simple σ-orbits are pairwise orthogonal within each orbit.
proofSteps: The sums β_O are linearly independent and span the fixed space: invariant simple coefficients are constant on orbits. Counting neighbors at a fixed node of T proves the displayed Cartan entries are integers and nonpositive.
For each O, the commuting product ∏_(i∈O)s_i restricts to reflection in β_O. These products preserve the set of root-orbit sums.

Descend the positive height of a root-orbit sum by such reflections using positive definiteness. If all resulting orbit roots become negative, the original orbit consists of the simple roots of that block. Thus every orbit sum is in the reflection orbit of a β_O.

Conversely those reflection orbits are orbit sums. This gives the generated finite root system, its base, reducedness and crystallographic axiom; Stembridge Claim 4 also proves all original root orbits are orthogonal under these finite hypotheses.

sources.match: Under orthogonality of simple orbits, orbit sums give the finite folded roots and their reflection group is the fixed Weyl subgroup.

acceptance: This construction is not applied to adjacent simple orbits, nor to affine or indefinite systems.
The Cartan denominator is |T| (column-coroot convention), not |O|.

nodes.title: Weyl group of an orthogonal fold
nodes.statement: For the orthogonal fold, restriction gives an isomorphism W(Φ)^σ ≃ W(Ψ). Its inverse sends the simple reflection of β_O to ∏_(i∈O)s_i. Here W(Φ)^σ is the fixed subgroup under conjugation by σ, not the pointwise stabilizer of E^σ.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
The hypotheses of orthogonal-fold hold.
proofSteps: The reflection comparison proves that the block products act as the folded simple reflections.

For a nonidentity fixed w choose a simple inversion using the pinned simple-descent theorem. Its entire simple σ-orbit consists of inversions. The reflections in that block commute and fix the other simple roots of the block, so each successive multiplication removes one inversion, by the pinned inversion-cardinality theorem. The total drop is |O|. The block product is fixed by σ; induct on inversion cardinality. No unplanned parabolic normal-form theorem is used.

Restriction is injective on the fixed subgroup: choose a strictly dominant vector and sum its finite σ-orbit to get a strictly dominant fixed vector. Existence of the first vector follows by solving the nonsingular simple-coroot matrix on E. An element trivial on E^σ fixes this vector, so the existing chamber stabilizer theorem and empty-wall theorem imply that element is identity. Restriction contains every folded simple reflection and every fixed element is a product of block reflections, giving the isomorphism.

nodes.title: Adjacent folding of even A type
nodes.statement: For n≥1, realize A_(2n) in the coordinate-sum-zero subspace of R^(2n+1), with σ(e_a−e_b)=e_(2n+2−b)−e_(2n+2−a). Put f_i=e_i−e_(2n+2−i), 1≤i≤n. The distinct orbit sums are exactly {±f_i, ±f_i±f_j : i<j}; their base is f_i−f_(i+1) (i<n), f_n. This is the B_n root model, with the rank-one case identified directly with A1. Every f_i has squared norm 2.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
The based irreducible system is A_(2n) and σ is its nonidentity reversal. Coordinate indices here are one-based.
proofSteps: Use the existing type-A realization and its diagram automorphism. A root e_a−e_b with neither index central gives either ±(f_i−f_j), ±(f_i+f_j), or the fixed root ±f_i. A pair of roots meeting the central index n+1 also sums to ±f_i. These cases exhaust all roots.

The f_i are orthogonal. Thus the listed set is closed under its reflections, has the B_n Cartan matrix, and the stated base has the required signed integral expansions. This verifies the finite reduced crystallographic root axioms directly.
For i<n the simple orbit is orthogonal. For the middle adjacent orbit, α_n+α_(n+1)=f_n has squared norm 2 rather than 4. Compute its coroot by the Euclidean pairing formula.
For an invariant weight with original simple-coroot values d_i=d_(2n+1−i), the folded simple-coroot values are d_i (i<n) and 2d_n.

nodes.title: Diagonal transport around a component cycle
nodes.statement: Let C,σC,…,σ^(c−1)C be a cycle of irreducible components, c≥1, and τ=σ^c|C. The map D(u)=Σ_(r=0)^(c−1)σ^r u is a linear equivalence E_C^τ → (⊕_(r<c)E_(σ^r C))^σ, inverse to projection to E_C. It takes τ-orbit sums to σ-orbit sums and multiplies squared norms by c. It identifies the simple-orbit cones and preserves all resulting Cartan pairings.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
Use the canonical σ-invariant form; distinct component spaces are orthogonal.
Components are connected components of the finite simple Cartan graph.
proofSteps: Distinct connected simple blocks are orthogonal. Positive-root descent shows every root belongs to one block: reflecting a simple root never leaves its connected block. The blocks span E, so they give an orthogonal direct sum of irreducible root systems.
A fixed vector is determined by its projection u onto the first block; the other projections are σ^r u and the closing condition is τu=u. This proves the formula, inverse and equivariance.
A τ-root orbit of size d yields a σ-orbit of size cd because roots in distinct components are distinct. Regroup that orbit sum to obtain D of the τ-orbit sum.
Orthogonality and σ-isometry give (D u,D v)=c(u,v); the common factor cancels from the coroot pairing formula. Simple coefficients transport without division.

nodes.title: Finite folding for every based diagram automorphism
nodes.statement: For any finite reduced crystallographic Φ and based automorphism σ, the SET Ψ of distinct root-orbit sums in E^σ, with simple roots the simple-orbit sums β_O, is a finite reduced crystallographic root system. It is the orthogonal direct sum of the return-map folds transported by D on component cycles. Every positive folded root is the sum of a positive root orbit. This is a theorem about orbit sums, with no assertion that orbit averages or restricted roots use the same normalization.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
σ is based; its preservation of the full Cartan matrix excludes length-exchanging graph permutations.
proofSteps: Use component-cycle to reduce to one irreducible return-map automorphism. Import the existing finite Dynkin classification and numbered diagram automorphisms.

Inspect the oriented finite Dynkin diagrams: irreducible B,C,F4,G2 have trivial based automorphism group. Nonidentity possibilities in A,D,E6 have orthogonal simple orbits except the reversal of A_(2n). D4 includes transpositions and three-cycles. For the identity on any nonsimply-laced type retain the original root system.

Apply orthogonal-fold in the first cases and adjacent-even-A-fold in the exceptional case. The elementary diagram inspection is part of this proof; it neither constructs a new classification nor changes the numbered automorphism API.

Transport along D, then take the orthogonal direct sum. The roots of an orthogonal direct sum are the union of the roots of its summands, not arbitrary sums across unrelated component cycles. Positivity and the stated base follow from the transported simple coefficients.

nodes.title: Invariant integral weights in the folded chamber
nodes.statement: If λ∈E^σ has integral original simple-coroot values, then it is integral for the folded system Ψ. Its folded simple-coroot value at β_O is the common original value d_O when the simple orbit is orthogonal, and 2d_O in the transported adjacent-middle even-A case. Therefore λ is original-dominant iff it is folded-dominant. The image of the invariant original weight lattice need not equal the full folded weight lattice.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
Use general-fold and its inherited form. For the reverse chamber equivalence, no assertion of reverse integrality is made.
proofSteps: σ-invariance makes the original coroot evaluations constant on each simple orbit.
For an orthogonal orbit O with common squared root length l², (β_O,β_O)=|O|l² and 2(λ,β_O)=|O|l²d_O. The ratio is d_O.
For the adjacent even-A orbit use the explicit doubled pairing. Component cycles scale numerator and denominator equally.

The multiplier is always a positive integer (1 or 2). This proves forward integrality and equivalence of signs, and hence equivalence of closed chambers. It does not divide a folded integral value by 2.

nodes.title: Invariant integral cone transport
nodes.statement: For δ∈E^σ, δ∈Q⁺(Φ,Δ) iff δ=Σ_O n_O β_O with n_O∈N, equivalently δ∈Q⁺(Ψ,B). The coefficients are unique. In particular, for original-integral invariant endpoints, integral dominance agrees with folded integral dominance. Also Q(Φ)^σ is exactly the embedded folded root lattice.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
Use general-fold and the identification of its simple root vectors inside E.
proofSteps: Expand δ in the linearly independent original simples. Applying σ permutes these coefficients; invariance and uniqueness force them to be constant on each orbit.
Regroup the sum once per distinct simple orbit; n_O is that common coefficient, with no division by |O|.
Conversely expand each β_O as its defining sum; natural coefficients stay natural. The same argument with integer coefficients gives the root-lattice equality.

nodes.title: Existential dominant orbit-sum step
nodes.statement: Let λ,μ∈L be distinct σ-fixed dominant integral weights with RootLE(λ,μ). There exists α∈Φ⁺ such that β=OrbitSum(σ,α) is nonzero, λ+β is σ-fixed, dominant and in L, and λ<_Qλ+β≤_Qμ. The choice is existential; it is not valid to sum an arbitrary orbit of individually allowable roots.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
σ is based and preserves L.
proofSteps: Use invariant-weight-transport and invariant-cone-transport to regard the endpoints as dominant integral weights of the finite folded system. Apply stembridge-step there.

Use generalFold_roots to lift the positive folded root to a positive original root orbit. Sign is constant on an original orbit because σ is based, so a positive folded root cannot come from a negative orbit.
Its orbit sum lies in Q⊆L and is σ-fixed. Transport the dominant condition and the remaining integral cone budget back to Φ. Positivity makes the lower comparison strict.

For cocharacters apply the statement to the COROOT system, with λ tested by the original roots. A choice of a short relative-root lift in an adjacent case, and all maps of root subgroups, are separate consumer interfaces.

nodes.title: Coroot step with central directions retained
nodes.statement: Let P be a finite reduced crystallographic real root pairing in finite-dimensional perfectly paired weight spaces V,V*, not necessarily spanned by the roots. Let σ be a P-automorphism preserving the base, and let λ,μ in a σ-stable subgroup L⊆V be fixed, dominant, integral on simple coroots, and distinct with μ−λ∈Q⁺. Assume Q⊆L. Then the conclusion of invariant-step holds in V. Apply P=the flipped real root pairing of a reductive root datum to obtain the integral positive-COROOT orbit step on its actual cocharacter lattice, preserving the common central component.
hypotheses: Finiteness, reducedness and crystallographicity concern the root set.
The ambient pairing is perfect; the induced finite root system on its real span has the canonical positive form. No finite-order assumption on σ on extra central directions is imposed.
proofSteps: Put E=span_R Φ and Z=the common kernel of all simple-coroot functionals. The symmetrized Cartan form is positive definite on E, hence the simple-coroot evaluation matrix on its simple basis is nonsingular. Solve this finite linear system to get V=E⊕Z and projection p preserving every simple-coroot evaluation. This uses only root-span positivity; it does not assert the canonical form is positive definite on V.
The decomposition is σ-stable: σ preserves roots and their coroot pairings. Thus pλ,pμ are fixed and retain the endpoint simple-coroot values. Since μ−λ∈E, pμ−pλ=μ−λ≠0.
Apply invariant-step on E with its full integral weight subgroup. The projected endpoints need not belong to the original L; their integral coroot values are all that is used.

The resulting increment β is in Q⊆L. Adding it to the ORIGINAL λ keeps the Z-component and lies below the ORIGINAL μ with the same integral difference budget. All simple-coroot values agree with those on E.

For a cocharacter lattice apply the entire construction to the dual pairing and the dual base. Work on the real span only inside this proof; the output is the sum of actual coroots in the original lattice.

The affine direction needs an extended affine action, Bruhat/Demazure and twisted Newton reduction; the modular direction needs integral representations and characteristic-p root operators. sourceIssues.reason: In D4 with central node 2 and triality on 1,3,4, take λ=2ρ, μ=λ+θ, θ=(1,2,1,1) in simple-root coordinates. suggestedShape.reason: The new folded carriers and their construction APIs are roadmap targets in the reader. Introducing placeholder data structures or proving a preliminary development to express them would violate the compact shape. The final orbit-sum theorem can already be stated over the original pinned carrier.

upstreamNotes: The reviewed RootSystems link packet notes inconsistent prose ownership of the general weight-lattice dictionary between RootSystems and LieHighestWeight. This finite plan avoids that ambiguity by using pinned cones and explicit integral coroot values; the general dictionary is not replanned.

The base RootSystems roadmap supplies finite Coxeter theory, not a full extended affine Iwahori–Weyl carrier. The proposed affine design must audit ReductiveGroupsPartII adapters and keep their full central action, rather than interpreting finite Weyl notation as that supplier.
